units.issue: RBI/Central Government moratorium and reconstruction or amalgamation of a banking company
units.date_scope: Supplied official consolidation as amended through 2021; the text records 2020 amendments effective 26.06.2020; historical-version applicability is otherwise unverified.
units.procedure_scope: RBI application and scheme preparation, Central Government moratorium and sanction, and statutory effects of a sanctioned scheme.

conditions.text: If the Reserve Bank considers that there is good reason, it may apply to the Central Government for a moratorium order concerning a banking company.
conditions.quote:
where it appears to the Reserve Bank that there is good reason so to do, the 
Reserve Bank may apply to the Central Government for an order of moratorium in 
respect of 3[a banking company].

conditions.text: After considering the Reserve Bank application, the Central Government may impose a moratorium on actions and proceedings, but the total moratorium period may not exceed six months.
conditions.quote:
The Central Government, after considering the application made by the Reserve 
Bank section -section (1), may make an order of moratorium staying the 
commencement or continuance of all actions and proceedings against the company 
for a fixed period of time on such terms and conditions as it thinks fit and proper 
and may from time to time extend the period so however that the total period of 
moratorium shall not exceed six months.

conditions.text: During a moratorium, unless Central Government directions provide otherwise, the banking company may not make depositor payments, discharge creditor liabilities or obligations, grant loans or advances, or make investments in credit instruments.
conditions.quote:
Except as otherwise provided by any directions given by the Central 
Government in the order made by it under sub-section (2) or at any time thereafter 
the banking company shall not during the period of moratorium make any payment 
to any depositors or discharge any liabilities or obligations to any other 
creditors 
13[or grant any loans or advances or make investments in any credit 
instruments].

conditions.text: The Reserve Bank may prepare a reconstruction or amalgamation scheme when it is satisfied that doing so is necessary in the public interest, depositor interests, proper management, or the interests of the banking system as a whole.
conditions.quote:
(a) in the public interest; or 
(b) in the interests of the depositors; or 
(c) in order to secure the proper management of the banking company; or 
(d) in the interests of the banking system of the country as a whole, 
it is necessary so to do, the Reserve Bank may prepare a scheme- 
(i) for the reconstruction of the banking company, or 
(ii) for the amalgamation of the banking company with any other banking 
institution (in this section referred to as "the transferee bank").]

conditions.text: The scheme must be placed before the Central Government for sanction; once sanctioned, it comes into force on the date or dates specified by the Central Government.
conditions.quote:
The scheme shall thereafter be placed before the Central Government for its 
sanction and the Central Government may sanction the scheme without any 
modifications or with such modifications as it may consider necessary, and the 
scheme as sanctioned by the Central Government shall come into force on such 
date as the Central Government may specify in this behalf: 
Provided that different dates may be specified for different provisions of the 
scheme.

Section 45 authorizes and governs schemes; a particular reconstruction or amalgamation still depends on the terms of the individual sanctioned scheme.

units.issue: Specific amalgamation and transfer of New Bank of India into Punjab National Bank
units.act: New Bank of India (Amalgamation and Transfer of Undertaking) Scheme, 1993, made under section 9 of the Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1980
units.date_scope: The Scheme is dated 4 September 1993, and the supplied notification appoints 4 September 1993 as its commencement date.
units.procedure_scope: Specific statutory scheme governing vesting of the New Bank of India undertaking in Punjab National Bank and related contracts, proceedings, and employees.

conditions.text: The Central Government appointed 4 September 1993 as the date on which the Scheme came into force.
conditions.quote:
the Central Government hereby
specifies the 4th day of September, 1993 as the appointed
date on which the aforesaid Scheme shall come into force.

conditions.text: On commencement of the Scheme, the undertakings of New Bank of India are transferred to and vest in Punjab National Bank.
conditions.quote:
3. Undertaking of New Bank of India to vest in Punjab
National Bank.—O»i the commencement of this Scheme, th*
undertakings of New Bank of India shall be transferred to.
and shall vest in, Punjab National Bank.

conditions.text: Unless the Scheme expressly provides otherwise, subsisting contracts and other instruments involving the transferor bank continue in full force against or in favor of the transferee bank.
conditions.quote:
Unless otherwise expressly provided by this Scheme, all
contracts, deeds, bonds, agreements, powers of attorney,
grants of legal representation and other instruments of what-
ever nature subsisting or having elfect, immediately before
the commencement of this Scheme and to which the transferor
bunk is a party or which are in favour of the transferor bank,
shall be of full force and effect against or in favour of the
transferee bank, and may be enforced or acted upon as fully
and effectively as if in the place of the transferor bank the
transferee bank had been a party thereto or as if they had
bee;i issued in favour of the transferee bank.

conditions.text: A suit, appeal, or other proceeding pending by or against the transferor bank immediately before commencement does not abate or become prejudicially affected by the transfer and may continue by or against the transferee bank.
conditions.quote:
If, immediately before the commencement of this
Scheme, any suit, appeal or other proceedings of whatever
nature in relation to any business of the undertakings which
have been transferred under clause 3, is pending by or against
the transferor bank, the same shall not abate, he discontinued
or be, in any way. prejudicially affected by reason of the
transfer of the undertakings of the transferor bank or of
anything contained in this Scheme but the suit, appeal or
other proceeding may be continued, prosecuted and enforced
by or Hgainst the transferee bank.

conditions.text: Subject to the Scheme and stated availability qualification, officers and employees of the transferor bank become officers or employees of the transferee bank on commencement and retain the specified service terms and benefits until duly changed or terminated.
conditions.quote:
Save as otherwise provided in this Scheme, every officer
or other employee of the transferor bank shall become, on
the commencement of this Scheme an officer or other emp-
loyee, as the case may be, of the transferee bank and shall
hold his office or service in that bank on the same terms
and conditions and with the same rights to pension, gratuity
and other matters as would have been admissible to him
if the undertakings of the transferor bank had not been
transferred to and vested in the transferee bank subject,
however, to such facilities being available at the time of.
the transfer to similarly placed officers and employees of
the transferee bank and continue to do so unless and until
his employment in the transferee bank is terminated or until
his remuneration, terms or conditions are duly altered by
the transferee bank.

limitations: This is a specific New Bank of India to Punjab National Bank scheme and has no automatic application to other bank mergers.

units.issue: Lawfulness and consent requirements for subletting or transfer of tenancy rights
units.date_scope: The supplied text distinguishes subletting before 9 June 1952, subletting on or after 9 June 1952, and conduct after commencement of the Act; the commencement date itself is not supplied.
units.procedure_scope: Substantive statutory treatment of subletting, assignment, and landlord consent; no target-case judicial interpretation is supplied.

conditions.text: A subletting made before 9 June 1952 is deemed lawful despite lack of landlord consent if the sub-tenant is in occupation at commencement of the Act.
conditions.quote: (1) Where at any time before the 9th day of June, 1952, a tenant has sub-let the whole or any part of the premises and the sub-tenant is, at the commencement of this Act, in occupation of such premises, then notwithstanding that the consent of the landlord was not obtained for such sub-letting, the premises shall be deemed to have been lawfully sub-let.

conditions.text: A subletting made on or after 9 June 1952 without the landlord's written consent is not deemed lawful.
conditions.quote: (2) No premises which have been sub-let either in whole or in part on or after the 9th day of June, 1952, without obtaining the consent in writing of the landlord, shall be deemed to have been lawfully sub-let.

conditions.text: After commencement of the Act, a tenant may neither sublet nor transfer or assign tenancy rights without the landlord's previous written consent.
conditions.quote: (3) After the commencement of this Act, no tenant shall, without the previous consent in writing of the landlord, -(a) sub-let the whole or any part of the premises held by him as a tenant; or(b) transfer or assign his rights in the tenancy or in any part thereof.

conditions.text: A landlord may not demand or receive a premium, pugree, or other consideration for consenting to subletting.
conditions.quote: (4) No landlord shall claim or receive the payment of any sum as premium or pugree or claim or receive any consideration whatsoever in cash or in kind for giving his consent to the sub-letting of the whole or any part of the premises held by the tenant.
